q: The Ruelle-Takens route to turbulence (1971) proposes that turbulence arises via a sequence of bifurcations: fixed point → periodic → 2-torus → (potentially chaotic) strange attractor. The key insight was that:
opts: After two Hopf bifurcations (creating a 2-torus), a third bifurcation generically leads to strange attractors (unlike the Landau-Hopf route via infinite Hopf bifurcations)
Turbulence requires infinitely many degrees of freedom
The route always goes through period-doubling
exp: Ruelle-Takens: generically, a 3-torus T³ (three incommensurate frequencies) supports strange attractors for arbitrary small perturbations — 3-frequency quasi-periodicity is not robust. This suggested turbulence can arise after few bifurcations, contrasting Landau's infinite-cascade hypothesis. Newhouse-Ruelle-Takens formalized this.
